deposit.value: Cap of 1.5 months' rent for all security and prepaid rent (tenant may voluntarily prepay more). Within 14 days, excluding weekends and holidays, after move-out and tenant demand, landlord must send itemized deductions and refund; wrongful withholding risks twice the amount withheld.
deposit.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1321(A) 1.5-month cap; (D) 14 business days itemized list; (E) double damages.

notice.value: Month-to-month: written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice; week-to-week: 10 days. Either side may give it.
notice.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1375(A) week-to-week 10 days; (B) month-to-month 30 days before periodic rental date.

rluipa.value: Federal law: zoning may not substantially burden religious exercise without a compelling reason, must treat religious assemblies on equal terms with secular ones, and may not exclude them outright.
rluipa.evidence: Federal field already verified; not re-read in this AZ lane.

yigby.value: No YIGBY law. HB 2815 (2024) and HB 2191 (2025, single-family homes on church land) did not become law; SB 1096 (2026, senior living on religious sites) was prefiled. Current A.R.S. 9-462.15 is an unrelated assisted-living section, so church-land housing needs normal zoning.
yigby.evidence: Read SB1096 prefiled and HB2191 engrossed texts; Title 9 index has no religious-housing section; bill status pages not read.

hoa_law.value: Planned communities (ch. 16) and condos (ch. 9): owners may rent unless the declaration bans it and must follow its rental-period limits; HOA may only ask tenant names, contacts, lease dates, vehicles; $25 fee cap. Solar devices cannot be banned (33-1816). Listed flags and for-sale/rent signs protected (33-1808, 33-1261). Free records review in 10 business days (33-1805).

permit.value: Annual STR permit from Planning & Development required before renting or advertising ($250 new/renewal). Application needs TPT licence, $500,000 insurance (or platform cover), Maricopa assessor rental registration, emergency contact, safety-equipment map; decision within 7 days. Certified-mail notice to neighbours and to HOAs/neighbourhood groups within 600 ft.

primary_residence.value: Not required in general. Only where the lot has an ADU with a certificate of occupancy issued on or after 14 Sep 2024 must the owner attest to living on the property; state law allows nothing broader.

zones.value: Allowed wherever a dwelling is allowed: state law bars cities from banning STRs or zoning them differently from other residential property. Event-centre, banquet, retail and other nonresidential uses of an STR are banned.
zones.evidence: A.R.S. 9-500.39(A),(B),(K); Phoenix 10-193 'event center' and 'special event' definitions.

caps.value: None. State preemption forbids prohibiting STRs or regulating them by classification, use or occupancy, so no count, density or night caps exist. Each unit on a property needs its own permit.
caps.evidence: A.R.S. 9-500.39(A)-(B); Phoenix 10-197(B) separate application per unit.

max_occupancy.value: No STR-specific guest cap (state preempts occupancy-based STR rules). General dwelling standard in the Neighborhood Preservation Ordinance applies: 250 sq ft for the first two occupants plus 150 sq ft per extra person; children under 13 not counted.
max_occupancy.evidence: Phoenix Code 39-5(E) space standard read; its application to STR guests not stated in code.

hostel_shared.value: STR definition covers owner-occupied homes offered to transients, so renting rooms is possible, but the zoning code caps a single-family dwelling at two guestrooms, each for at most two non-family persons, no cooking. Six or more lodgers is a boarding house needing a use permit outside single-family zones.
hostel_shared.evidence: 10-193 STR definition; ZO 202 'Guestroom'; ZO 608 note 3 (max two guestrooms) and boarding house row.

taxes.value: State TPT licence required and its number must appear on ads. Transient lodging (stays under 30 days): state+Maricopa County 7.27%, Phoenix hotel 2.8% plus 3% additional = about 13.07%. Platforms collect the state/county share when facilitated.

listing_id.value: Yes. Every ad must show the Phoenix STR permit number and a notice that owner, renter and guest may owe up to $2,000 for police response to parties; permit posted within 10 ft of the main entrance. Platforms must require the permit number (fine up to $2,500/day).

pending.value: Code amended again in 2026 (Ord. G-7495, ADU residency attestation). State law caps penalties: $500/$1,000/$3,500 or 1-3 nights' rent; suspension up to 12 months after three verified violations. No pending STR litigation or vote found.
pending.evidence: 10-197 history note G-7495 (2026); 10-202; A.R.S. 9-500.39(F); negative finding not exhaustive.

registration.value: Owners of any residential rental must register with the Maricopa County Assessor (owner, address, parcel, year built; out-of-state owners name an in-state agent); unregistered units may not be occupied; city civil penalties up to $150/day. Cities may not run their own rental registration or licensing.
registration.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1902(A)-(C),(G); 9-1304(B)-(C); Maricopa Assessor Rental Registration page.

family.value: Family = any number of related persons (blood, marriage, adoption) plus servants, or up to five unrelated persons, living as one housekeeping unit.
family.evidence: Phoenix Zoning Ordinance Sec. 202 'Family' definitions 1 and 2.

per_bedroom.value: Floor-area rule, not per bedroom: at least 250 sq ft of gross dwelling area for the first two occupants and 150 sq ft per additional occupant; children under 13 excluded.
per_bedroom.evidence: Neighborhood Preservation Ordinance 39-5(E) Space and occupancy standards.

adu.value: Two ADUs allowed with one single-family home (one attached, one detached), a third if one is affordable on a lot of 1 acre+. Size: up to 75% of the house and 1,000 sq ft (lots over 10,000 sq ft: lesser of 3,000 sq ft or 10% of lot). Setbacks 3 ft side/rear. State mandate A.R.S. 9-461.18 applies.
adu.evidence: ZO 608 note 2 (two ADUs, third affordable); ZO 706.A.2-8; A.R.S. 9-461.18(A),(B).

shed.value: Accessory structures that are not ADUs have their own setbacks and height limits; living space must meet ADU rules (own sleeping and sanitation, Sec. 706.A). No specific shed-occupancy ban read.
shed.evidence: ZO 706.A vs 706.B accessory structures; ZO 202 ADU definitions.

tent.value: No explicit private-lot tent rule found. RV parks are the zoning use for tents and similar temporary living quarters, and a tent is not a listed dwelling in residential districts.
tent.evidence: ZO 202 'Recreational Vehicle Park' definition (tents included); 608 residential use table.

rv.value: Occupied RVs must be in a recreational vehicle park (C-1 to C-3 by special permit, max 20 spaces/acre), except hospital parking; a mobile home may be lived in during home construction only by use permit for up to one year.
rv.evidence: ZO 701 item 8 occupied RV in RV park; 647.A.2.g RV parks.

thow.value: 'Park model' (up to 400 sq ft, on wheels, ANSI) expressly includes tiny homes and is treated with RVs, so a wheeled tiny home is lived in only in an RV park; a tiny home on a foundation can be an ADU.
thow.evidence: ZO 202 'Park Model' and 'Recreational Vehicle Park' definitions; ZO 701 item 8.

rooming.value: Rooming house = group home. Boarding house (6+ unrelated lodgers paying per room) is not allowed in single-family districts; use permit in multifamily districts, 1,320 ft spacing, 25% lot coverage, 100 sq ft open space per bed, arterial/collector access.
rooming.evidence: ZO 202 'Boarding House', 'Rooming House'; ZO 608 use table and note 9.

coliving.value: Up to five unrelated adults may share a unit as a family; six or more is a boarding house or group home needing a use permit in multifamily zones. A.R.S. 9-462.13 middle-housing mandate (duplex-fourplex near downtown) applies to Phoenix.
coliving.evidence: ZO 202 Family; ZO 608 notes 9 and 18; A.R.S. 9-462.13(A); Phoenix implementing text not read.

hoa_data.value: No state HOA registry. Phoenix keeps a registry of HOAs and neighbourhood associations (STR owners must notify those within 600 ft); declarations are recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder.
hoa_data.evidence: Phoenix 10-199(E) HOAs registered with Neighborhood Services; registry itself not downloaded.

worship_zoning.value: 'Church/Place of Worship' is permitted by right in every residential district; accessory uses allowed with conditions. Religious assembly may include rectory, dormitory, school and day care. Housing beyond that needs the district's residential rules.
worship_zoning.evidence: ZO 608 use table row Church/Place of Worship 'p' all districts; ZO 202 'Religious Assembly'.

deposit.value: Cap of 1.5 months' rent for all security and prepaid rent (tenant may voluntarily prepay more). Within 14 days, excluding weekends and holidays, after move-out and tenant demand, landlord must send itemized deductions and refund; wrongful withholding risks twice the amount withheld.
deposit.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1321(A) 1.5-month cap; (D) 14 business days itemized list; (E) double damages.

notice.value: Month-to-month: written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice; week-to-week: 10 days. Either side may give it.
notice.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1375(A) week-to-week 10 days; (B) month-to-month 30 days before periodic rental date.

rluipa.value: Federal law: zoning may not substantially burden religious exercise without a compelling reason, must treat religious assemblies on equal terms with secular ones, and may not exclude them outright.
rluipa.evidence: Federal field already verified; not re-read in this AZ lane.

yigby.value: No YIGBY law. HB 2815 (2024) and HB 2191 (2025, single-family homes on church land) did not become law; SB 1096 (2026, senior living on religious sites) was prefiled. Current A.R.S. 9-462.15 is an unrelated assisted-living section, so church-land housing needs normal zoning.
yigby.evidence: Read SB1096 prefiled and HB2191 engrossed texts; Title 9 index has no religious-housing section; bill status pages not read.

hoa_law.value: Planned communities (ch. 16) and condos (ch. 9): owners may rent unless the declaration bans it and must follow its rental-period limits; HOA may only ask tenant names, contacts, lease dates, vehicles; $25 fee cap. Solar devices cannot be banned (33-1816). Listed flags and for-sale/rent signs protected (33-1808, 33-1261). Free records review in 10 business days (33-1805).

permit.value: Annual city vacation rental licence ($250) required since 8 Jan 2023, one per dwelling unit; issued within 7 business days. Needs TPT licence, 24-hour emergency contact, background attestations, $500,000 insurance (or platform cover) and written neighbour notice. Operating without one: fine of at least $1,000.

primary_residence.value: Not required, except an ADU with a certificate of occupancy issued on or after 14 Sep 2024 may be an STR only if the owner lives on the property as a primary residence. Restricted-affordable ADUs may never be STRs.

zones.value: Single-family dwellings 'including vacation rental or short-term rental' are permitted in residential districts; state law bars bans. Nonresidential uses (event centre, banquet, retail, sober living, adult business) prohibited.

caps.value: No numeric or density cap; state law preempts caps. A separate licence is needed for each house or dwelling unit.

max_occupancy.value: Required door notice states occupancy is limited to one family: one to six adults plus their related dependent children (zoning 'family' definition). With ADUs, the whole lot is capped at six adults.
max_occupancy.evidence: Code 18-175(h) notice item 9; Zoning Ord. 3.100 Family; 7.904.A.3.

hostel_shared.value: Not provided for. An STR is a dwelling rented under 30 days; lodging in non-dwelling buildings is 'travel accommodation' (commercial). Occupancy is capped at six adults, and minors may not rent.
hostel_shared.evidence: Zoning 3.100 'Vacation rental', 'Travel accommodation'; Code 18-178 juveniles; no hostel rule found.

taxes.value: State TPT licence required. Transient lodging: state+Maricopa County 7.27%, Scottsdale 1.7% plus 5% additional hotel/motel tax = about 13.97%. Platforms remit state/county tax for facilitated bookings.

listing_id.value: Yes. Every ad must list the city vacation rental licence number (minimum fine $500). Inside, post a laminated notice with licence number, local contact, banned uses and party rules, plus an egress/safety map.

pending.value: No pending litigation or vote found. Rules added: emergency contact must arrive in person within 1 hour (fines $250-$500), sex-offender check of booker 24 h before stays, juvenile rentals banned (2024), nuisance-party rules in Art. VIII.

registration.value: Owners of any residential rental must register with the Maricopa County Assessor; unregistered units may not be occupied; cities may fine but may not run their own rental registry or licence. STRs must also comply with assessor recording.

family.value: Family = one to six adults plus their related dependent children living as one housekeeping unit; state-licensed homes for people with developmental disabilities count as a family. 'Group home' = more than six adults sharing without care.

per_bedroom.value: No per-bedroom or floor-area occupancy rule found in the property maintenance article; the practical limit is the six-adult family definition (also lot-wide with ADUs).
per_bedroom.evidence: Code ch. 18 art. III searched; Zoning 3.100 Family; 7.904.A.3; building codes in ch. 31 not read.

adu.value: One attached and one detached ADU allowed on single-family lots (max two on lots under 1 acre; a third restricted-affordable one on 1 acre+). One may be 75% of the house or 1,000 sq ft, whichever less; others 500 sq ft. Separate meters, no separate sale; six adults total on the lot.

shed.value: A guest house is an accessory building for guests, not a dwelling: max half the house's floor area, no separate meter, never rented separately (deed restriction). Full-time living space needs an ADU approval.
shed.evidence: Table 5.102 note 6 guest house; Zoning 3.100 Guest house and ADU definitions.

tent.value: No tent-living rule found. Land may be used only for listed uses; residential tables list one main dwelling, ADUs and guest houses, not tents.
tent.evidence: Zoning Ord. 7.300 uses limited to those permitted; Table 5.102; no explicit tent text located.

rv.value: RVs are vehicles; no zoning use lets people live in one on a residential lot, and only listed uses are allowed. Specific RV-occupancy ban not located.
rv.evidence: Zoning 3.100 'Vehicle' includes campers and RVs; 7.300; Table 5.102.

thow.value: Not a listed dwelling type; a tiny home must meet ADU or dwelling rules (own sleeping, kitchen, sanitary facilities, building code). Wheeled units fall under vehicles.
thow.evidence: Zoning 3.100 'Dwelling unit', 'Accessory Dwelling Unit', 'Vehicle'; no tiny-home text.

rooming.value: 'Rooming house' points to 'boardinghouse', which has no definition in the current code, and group homes of more than six unrelated adults are not listed uses in single-family districts.
rooming.evidence: Zoning 3.100 'Rooming house. See boardinghouse'; Table 5.102 lacks group home.

coliving.value: Up to six unrelated adults may share a dwelling. Larger groups are 'group homes', not permitted in single-family districts. Middle housing mandate (A.R.S. 9-462.13) applies (Scottsdale over 75,000).
coliving.evidence: Zoning 3.100 Family, Group home; A.R.S. 9-462.13(A); local middle-housing text not read.

hoa_data.value: No state HOA registry; HOAs are usually Arizona nonprofit corporations (Corporation Commission filings) and declarations are recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder. No Scottsdale HOA list found.
hoa_data.evidence: Background; no registry dataset located this session.

worship_zoning.value: Place of worship permitted by right in single-family districts with standards: 20,000 sq ft minimum lot, FAR 0.20, 30 ft height (Design Review), collector-or-greater access, lights off 10 pm, no outdoor speakers. Permitted in commercial districts too.
worship_zoning.evidence: Table 5.102 row 18 and note 8; Art. XI commercial land use table.

str_preemption.value: Cities and counties may not ban STRs or regulate them by classification, use or occupancy. They may require a permit (max $250, decision in 7 business days), emergency contact, neighbour notice, licence number on ads, $500,000 insurance, owner residence only for post-9/14/2024 ADUs; fines $500-$3,500 and suspensions up to 12 months.
str_preemption.evidence: A.R.S. 9-500.39(A)-(G),(K); 11-269.17 county twin listed in Title 11 index (not read).

rent_control.value: Rent control on private residential property is preempted statewide; cities, including charter cities, may not control rents. Exception: housing owned, financed, insured or subsidised by state or local government.

deposit.value: Cap of 1.5 months' rent for all security and prepaid rent (tenant may voluntarily prepay more). Within 14 days, excluding weekends and holidays, after move-out and tenant demand, landlord must send itemized deductions and refund; wrongful withholding risks twice the amount withheld.
deposit.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1321(A) 1.5-month cap; (D) 14 business days itemized list; (E) double damages.

notice.value: Month-to-month: written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice; week-to-week: 10 days. Either side may give it.
notice.evidence: A.R.S. 33-1375(A) week-to-week 10 days; (B) month-to-month 30 days before periodic rental date.

ltr_registration.value: Yes, via county assessor: every residential rental owner must keep owner, parcel and year-built data with the assessor (out-of-state owners name an in-state agent; fee max $10); unregistered rentals may not be occupied. Cities and counties may not adopt their own rental registration or licensing.

source_of_income.value: State fair housing law does not list source of income. No state preemption found; Phoenix protects source of income (incl. vouchers) by city ordinance since 2023, Scottsdale does not.
source_of_income.evidence: A.R.S. 41-1491.14 protected classes; Phoenix Code 18-11 et seq. (Ord. G-7086); preemption search not exhaustive.

occupancy_law.value: Cities over 75,000 must allow one attached and one detached ADU by right, rentable long-term, no owner-occupancy or parking rules (9-461.18); duplex-fourplex/townhomes near downtown (9-462.13); housing on obsolete commercial sites in cities 150,000+ (9-462.10). Assisted living homes of 10 or fewer cannot be capped (9-462.15).

hoa_law.value: Planned communities (ch. 16) and condos (ch. 9): owners may rent unless the declaration bans it and must follow its rental-period limits; HOA may only ask tenant names, contacts, lease dates, vehicles; $25 fee cap. Solar devices cannot be banned (33-1816). Listed flags and for-sale/rent signs protected (33-1808, 33-1261). Free records review in 10 business days (33-1805).

hoa_registry.value: No statewide HOA registry found. Associations are typically nonprofit corporations filed with the Arizona Corporation Commission; declarations are recorded by county recorders. Owners must get free records access within 10 business days.
hoa_registry.evidence: Negative finding; A.R.S. 33-1805(A) records access read.

yigby.value: No YIGBY law. HB 2815 (2024) and HB 2191 (2025, single-family homes on church land) did not become law; SB 1096 (2026, senior living on religious sites) was prefiled. Current A.R.S. 9-462.15 is an unrelated assisted-living section, so church-land housing needs normal zoning.
yigby.evidence: Read SB1096 prefiled and HB2191 engrossed texts; Title 9 index has no religious-housing section; bill status pages not read.
